Each prompt starts with a <task-instructions> block saying what that prompt is for and what it may change. Its code is located in ./src.

Its spec's Piton source, in ./spec, is only where edits to the spec go.

Read the spec from its compiled reference under .claude/reference, where inheritance, expressions, and links are already resolved, or, for one thing, from what `piton slice` prints for it with this harness's adapter.

Never read the .pi source under ./spec to learn what the spec says; that is only where edits to the spec go.

Read only what the change depends on, and start the work as soon as you have. Links to .claude/reference/... in the prompt are the spec for what they name: read those, and then only the pages they link to that the change actually depends on. Don't survey the spec, list its folders, or search it before you start. A page the prompt already gives you as a slice is already read: never read it again. Don't re-read anything you've already read.

content.text:
Suspense compiles again. The break was in `render_tabs` in `src/prompt_mode.rs`, in the code that drags a file tab along the tab bar. It had been pasted twice: the first copy ended in an `on_drop` holding the drag-start code, which was the error at line 3975, and a second, less-indented copy followed. I replaced both with the single drag, hover and drop sequence from HEAD, at the right indentation.

That damage was already there before my change. My scroll edits in that file are only in `select_tab`, `open_planning` and the project switch.

To confirm it, I ran `cargo check` on a scratch copy of the crate, and it finished with no errors and only five unused-code warnings. A full build in the repo itself can't get through here, because this environment can't read the prompt files under `.suspense/system-prompts`. On your machine those load normally. I didn't run the app or the tests.
